content.text: Checking the compiled JS for how the manager reaches SQL storage.

In the installed `agents` 0.27.0, you don't pass `MCPClientManager` any storage. Its constructor takes only `(name, version, options?)`, and `options` holds just `env` and `createAuthProvider` (`node_modules/agents/dist/agent-routing-Bhdbvf7s.d.ts:2743-2803`). The manager is a `LifecycleCapability`, so it uses the storage of the Lifecycle it's installed on. In practice that's the host Agent's Durable Object storage: its `sql()` helper runs `this.lifecycle.storage.sql.exec(...)` (`node_modules/agents/dist/client-1tEQ1Oqz.js:1352-1353`).

Server registrations are saved in the `cf_agents_mcp_servers` SQLite table in that Durable Object. `onStart()` reads them back to restore HTTP and RPC connections after the object wakes from hibernation. On an Agent you normally reach it through `this.mcp` rather than creating one yourself.
